27:84.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُو قَالَ أَكَذَّبۡتُم بِـَٔايَٰتِي وَلَمۡ تُحِيطُواْ بِهَا عِلۡمًا أَمَّاذَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
27:84.en: Until, when they arrive [at the place of Judgement], He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you encompassed them not in knowledge, or what [was it that] you were doing

27:85.ar: وَوَقَعَ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ عَلَيۡهِم بِمَا ظَلَمُواْ فَهُمۡ لَا يَنطِقُونَ
27:85.en: And the decree will befall them for the wrong they did, and they will not [be able to] speak

28:71.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍۚ أَفَلَا تَسۡمَعُونَ
28:71.en: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear

28:72.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِلَيۡلࣲ تَسۡكُنُونَ فِيهِۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
28:72.en: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see

28:73.ar: وَمِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
28:73.en: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and [by day] seek from His bounty and [that] perhaps you will be grateful

28:74.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُنَادِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُ أَيۡنَ شُرَكَآءِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ
28:74.en: And [warn of] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are my 'partners' which you used to claim

28:75.ar: وَنَزَعۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةࣲ شَهِيدࣰ ا فَقُلۡنَا هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَٰنَكُمۡ فَعَلِمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ لِلَّهِ وَضَلَّ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
28:75.en: And We will extract from every nation a witness and say, "Produce your proof," and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is that which they used to invent

29:2.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
29:2.en: Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried

29:3.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۖ فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
29:3.en: But We have certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars

29:4.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ أَن يَسۡبِقُونَاۚ سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ
29:4.en: Or do those who do evil deeds think they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge

45:23.ar: أَفَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمࣲ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمۡعِهِۦ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِۦ غِشَٰوَةࣰ فَمَن يَهۡدِيهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
45:23.en: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded

25:43.ar: أَرَءَيۡتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِ وَكِيلًا
25:43.en: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him

1:5.en: It is You we worship and You we ask for help

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds of anything. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

3khsYni1WuU.speaker: adnan
3khsYni1WuU.speaker_note: single speaker in the sheikh's Ramadan nightly Quranic Themes series; mentions his own open-book courses and a Jumuah he gave on these verses
3khsYni1WuU.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 19: Difficult Questions
3khsYni1WuU.one_line: Three hard questions Allah poses in the Quran: what were you doing, where are My partners, and did you think you would not be tested?
3khsYni1WuU.summary: The Quran is full of questions, and some are meant to be hard so we prepare our answers now. Life itself, he argues, is answering questions, and Allah has handed us both the questions and the answers in advance. The catch is that these answers cannot be memorised; like the open-book method of the old scholars, who had students teach the book back, the deen is only mastered by understanding and living it, not by Googling. He takes three passages. In An-Naml, Allah asks those who rejected His signs without studying them what they were doing with their lives, and they are left speechless because only truth can be spoken that Day; he admits he has no answer of his own and can only hope not to be asked. In Al-Qasas, after reminding us that only Allah gives night and day, He asks where the partners are whom people loved, feared or obeyed like Him, including those who simply followed their desires, and demands their proof. In Al-Ankabut, He asks whether people thought they could say 'we believe' without being tested. Believers who expect protection from hardship misunderstand the equation: iman is a precious claim, words are free, and tests expose who is truthful. He asks people to prove their claim and pray for strength to carry their burdens.

outline.heading: Hold firm when others ease off
outline.gist: As the last ten nights approach many people relax; to be chosen by Allah you have to stand out by showing up, especially the young.

outline.heading: Difficult questions in the Quran
outline.gist: Some are painful to face honestly, some are asked on the Day of Judgment of the unprepared, some are complex; they are posed early to prepare us.

outline.heading: Life is answering questions
outline.gist: School, family and courts all ask hard questions; the Quran's are about what your life, time, wealth and choices were for, and whether your belief was genuine.

outline.heading: The answers are given, but they must be lived
outline.gist: Allah supplied the questions and answers in advance, yet saying the right answer is useless unless it became part of your identity; memorising for an exam does not work here.

outline.heading: Open book: how the scholars tested mastery
outline.gist: His courses are open-book because understanding is what counts; the old teachers had the student teach the book back and sent him to restudy if he could not explain it.

outline.heading: Mastered only by practice, not by Googling
outline.gist: This knowledge cannot be mastered without living it; reducing the deen to answers copied from a web page misses that.

outline.heading: Did you deny My signs without learning them?
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment Allah asks those who rejected His signs at face value; when they deny it, He asks them to explain what they were doing with their lives instead.

outline.heading: A life story he cannot defend
outline.gist: He says he could not justify his own book of deeds; how would anyone account for their youth, working years, strength and old age?

outline.heading: Silenced: only truth can be spoken that Day
outline.gist: The decree falls on them that they can only speak the truth, and because of their wrongdoing they have nothing to say.

outline.heading: If He asks the detailed questions
outline.gist: Like a lawyer going through your documents, Allah could ask about each day, blessing and choice; he can only pray not to be asked and to be found worthy of mercy.

outline.heading: Who brings light and night but Allah?
outline.gist: Before the story of Qarun, Allah asks who could bring light if night never ended, or rest if day never ended.

outline.heading: Where are My partners?
outline.gist: Allah asks to see those whose laws people treated as equal to His and whom they loved or feared as much or more; claiming many gods conveniently loosens ethics.

outline.heading: Taking desire as a god
outline.gist: No religion worships desire, yet the Quran twice describes the person who always does what he feels over justice, righteousness or empathy as having made desire his god.

outline.heading: You alone we worship: a claim to establish
outline.gist: When we say it in al-Fatihah Allah says this is between Him and His servant; it has to be proven by a life, not just recited.

outline.heading: Bring your proof: the truth belongs to Allah
outline.gist: A witness is brought from every nation and people are told to produce their evidence; they realise with certainty that truth is Allah's alone and their inventions vanish.

outline.heading: Did people think they would be left to say 'we believe'?
outline.gist: A real question at the start of Al-Ankabut, addressed to every one of us, about claiming iman.

outline.heading: Iman is a heavy claim
outline.gist: The Bedouins who claimed iman were told they had only entered Islam; the people in Al-Ankabut claim the higher level of proven commitment.

outline.heading: Expecting a red carpet for believers
outline.gist: He once thought giving up haram would shield him from hardship; asking 'why is this happening to me' shows a misreading of the equation.

outline.heading: Every nation before was tested
outline.gist: Every people who made the claim was tried, and Allah will make clear who is truthful.

outline.heading: Truthful whatever it costs
outline.gist: The truthful put Allah first even if it costs wealth, health or life; Allah will also expose the liars.

outline.heading: Evildoers who think they got away with it
outline.gist: Those who steal or commit zina and see no lightning bolt think they have outrun Allah; that is terrible judgment.

outline.heading: A precious claim words cannot carry
outline.gist: Iman of convenience will be shaken; Allah does not need our belief, yet eternal bliss is built on the claim, and like saying 'I love you' it means nothing without behaviour.

outline.heading: Tests are promised: ask for a stronger back
outline.gist: Testing is a divine promise; ask for tests you can pass, like his teacher who asked Allah not to lift his burden but to strengthen his back to carry it.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The approach of the last ten nights is when people relax, so it is the time to stand out with effort.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: The Quran gives us the questions of the Day of Judgment in advance; the hardest is how we spent our lives, and only lived answers will hold.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Islamic learning was always about comprehension and practice, tested by teaching back, not memorisation or quick online answers.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Partners with Allah include anything loved, feared or obeyed like Him, including one's own desires; on the Day there will be no proof for them.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Testing is the promised way Allah separates truthful believers from those who only claim iman.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Iman is a costly claim that must be proven in behaviour, not an inherited or convenient label.

themes.label: Sins, their causes and remedies
themes.note: Seeing no immediate consequence for sin leads people to think they have escaped Allah.

quran.point: The one who takes his desire as his god: living by feelings is a practical form of shirk.
The second place the Quran describes taking desire as a god.
You alone we worship and from You alone we seek help: a claim that must be established by how one lives.
The Bedouins told they had entered Islam but iman had not yet entered their hearts: iman is a higher claim.

hadith.gist: When the servant says in al-Fatihah 'You alone we worship and from You alone we seek help', Allah says: this is between Me and My servant.

maxims: Most of life is preparing good answers for difficult questions
Islam has always been open book
So much to answer for, so few answers worth offering
It costs nothing to say words
Iman of convenience will be tested

stories.who: Classical teachers who had students teach the book back
stories.point: Mastery is shown by explaining and applying, not by memorising.

stories.who: The sheikh's own youthful expectation of protection
stories.point: He once believed that leaving haram would bring a life free of hardship, before he understood that believers are promised tests.
Ask Allah not to remove the burden He chose for you but to strengthen your back to carry it.

contemporary: His open-book IDA courses
Reliance on answers looked up on the internet for religious questions
takeaways: Stay committed through the last ten nights when others ease off.
Study the deen to understand and live it rather than memorising or searching for quick answers.
Prepare now for the question of how you spent your life, youth, wealth and time.
Look for practical partners in your life: desires, people or laws you obey, love or fear more than Allah.
Expect tests as part of claiming iman and ask Allah for the strength to carry them.

20:2.en: We have not sent down to you the Qur'an that you be distressed

20:3.en: But only as a reminder for those who fear [Allah]

20:4.ar: تَنزِيلࣰ ا مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ ٱلۡعُلَى
20:4.en: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens

20:5.en: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established

20:6.ar: لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحۡتَ ٱلثَّرَىٰ
20:6.en: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil

20:7.ar: وَإِن تَجۡهَرۡ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَعۡلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ وَأَخۡفَى
20:7.en: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden

20:8.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰ
20:8.en: Allah - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names

20:9.en: And has the story of Moses reached you

20:10.ar: إِذۡ رَءَا نَارࣰ ا فَقَالَ لِأَهۡلِهِ ٱمۡكُثُوٓاْ إِنِّيٓ ءَانَسۡتُ نَارࣰ ا لَّعَلِّيٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنۡهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوۡ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدࣰ ى
20:10.en: When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance

20:11.en: And when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses

20:12.ar: إِنِّيٓ أَنَا۠ رَبُّكَ فَٱخۡلَعۡ نَعۡلَيۡكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلۡوَادِ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسِ طُوࣰ ى
20:12.en: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa

20:13.en: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you]

20:14.ar: إِنَّنِيٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعۡبُدۡنِي وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكۡرِيٓ
20:14.en: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance

20:15.ar: إِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ ءَاتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخۡفِيهَا لِتُجۡزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسِۭ بِمَا تَسۡعَىٰ
20:15.en: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives

20:16.ar: فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنۡهَا مَن لَّا يُؤۡمِنُ بِهَا وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ فَتَرۡدَىٰ
20:16.en: So do not let one avert you from it who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you [then] would perish

20:17.en: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses

20:18.ar: قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّؤُاْ عَلَيۡهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِي وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَـَٔارِبُ أُخۡرَىٰ
20:18.en: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses

20:20.en: So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly

20:21.ar: قَالَ خُذۡهَا وَلَا تَخَفۡۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا ٱلۡأُولَىٰ
20:21.en: [Allah] said, "Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition

20:22.ar: وَٱضۡمُمۡ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ تَخۡرُجۡ بَيۡضَآءَ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ سُوٓءٍ ءَايَةً أُخۡرَىٰ
20:22.en: And draw in your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign

20:23.en: That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs

20:24.en: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed

20:25.en: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand for me my breast [with assurance]

20:26.en: And ease for me my task

20:27.en: And untie the knot from my tongue

20:28.en: That they may understand my speech

20:29.ar: وَٱجۡعَل لِّي وَزِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَهۡلِي
20:29.en: And appoint for me a minister from my family

20:32.en: And let him share my task

20:33.en: That we may exalt You much

20:35.en: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing

20:36.en: [Allah] said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses

20:37.en: And We had already conferred favor upon you another time

20:38.ar: إِذۡ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
20:38.en: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired

20:39.ar: أَنِ ٱقۡذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقۡذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ فَلۡيُلۡقِهِ ٱلۡيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأۡخُذۡهُ عَدُوࣱّ لِّي وَعَدُوࣱّ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَلۡقَيۡتُ عَلَيۡكَ مَحَبَّةࣰ مِّنِّي وَلِتُصۡنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيۡنِيٓ
20:39.en: [Saying], 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me that you would be brought up under My eye

20:40.ar: إِذۡ تَمۡشِيٓ أُخۡتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكۡفُلُهُۥۖ فَرَجَعۡنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَيۡ تَقَرَّ عَيۡنُهَا وَلَا تَحۡزَنَۚ وَقَتَلۡتَ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَنَجَّيۡنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونࣰ اۚ فَلَبِثۡتَ سِنِينَ فِيٓ أَهۡلِ مَدۡيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئۡتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرࣲ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
20:40.en: [And We favored you] when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses

20:41.en: And I produced you for Myself

20:42.ar: ٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَأَخُوكَ بِـَٔايَٰتِي وَلَا تَنِيَا فِي ذِكۡرِي
20:42.en: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance

20:43.en: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed

20:44.ar: فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا لَّيِّنࣰ ا لَّعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوۡ يَخۡشَىٰ
20:44.en: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allah]

20:45.ar: قَالَا رَبَّنَآ إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَن يَفۡرُطَ عَلَيۡنَآ أَوۡ أَن يَطۡغَىٰ
20:45.en: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress

20:46.ar: قَالَ لَا تَخَافَآۖ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَآ أَسۡمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ
20:46.en: [Allah] said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see

20:47.ar: فَأۡتِيَاهُ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرۡسِلۡ مَعَنَا بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَا تُعَذِّبۡهُمۡۖ قَدۡ جِئۡنَٰكَ بِـَٔايَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكَۖ وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
20:47.en: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance

20:48.ar: إِنَّا قَدۡ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡنَآ أَنَّ ٱلۡعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
20:48.en: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away

20:49.en: [Pharaoh] said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses

20:50.ar: قَالَ رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِيٓ أَعۡطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلۡقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ
20:50.en: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]

20:51.en: [Pharaoh] said, "Then what is the case of the former generations

20:52.ar: قَالَ عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَٰبࣲۖ لَّا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنسَى
20:52.en: [Moses] said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets

20:53.ar: ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَهۡدࣰ ا وَسَلَكَ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا سُبُلࣰ ا وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا مِّن نَّبَاتࣲ شَتَّىٰ
20:53.en: [It is He] who has made for you the earth as a bed [spread out] and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants

20:54.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱرۡعَوۡاْ أَنۡعَٰمَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّأُوْلِي ٱلنُّهَىٰ
20:54.en: Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for those of intelligence

20:55.ar: ۞مِنۡهَا خَلَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمۡ وَمِنۡهَا نُخۡرِجُكُمۡ تَارَةً أُخۡرَىٰ
20:55.en: From the earth We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time

20:56.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا كُلَّهَا فَكَذَّبَ وَأَبَىٰ
20:56.en: And We certainly showed Pharaoh Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused

20:57.ar: قَالَ أَجِئۡتَنَا لِتُخۡرِجَنَا مِنۡ أَرۡضِنَا بِسِحۡرِكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
20:57.en: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses

20:58.ar: فَلَنَأۡتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحۡرࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦ فَٱجۡعَلۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكَ مَوۡعِدࣰ ا لَّا نُخۡلِفُهُۥ نَحۡنُ وَلَآ أَنتَ مَكَانࣰ ا سُوࣰ ى
20:58.en: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned

20:59.ar: قَالَ مَوۡعِدُكُمۡ يَوۡمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ وَأَن يُحۡشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحࣰ ى
20:59.en: [Moses] said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning

20:60.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فَجَمَعَ كَيۡدَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَتَىٰ
20:60.en: So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came [to Moses]

20:61.ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰ وَيۡلَكُمۡ لَا تَفۡتَرُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبࣰ ا فَيُسۡحِتَكُم بِعَذَابࣲۖ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰ
20:61.en: Moses said to the magicians summoned by Pharaoh, "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against Allah or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents [such falsehood]

20:62.en: So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation

20:63.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنۡ هَٰذَٰنِ لَسَٰحِرَٰنِ يُرِيدَانِ أَن يُخۡرِجَاكُم مِّنۡ أَرۡضِكُم بِسِحۡرِهِمَا وَيَذۡهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلۡمُثۡلَىٰ
20:63.en: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way

20:64.ar: فَأَجۡمِعُواْ كَيۡدَكُمۡ ثُمَّ ٱئۡتُواْ صَفࣰّ اۚ وَقَدۡ أَفۡلَحَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مَنِ ٱسۡتَعۡلَىٰ
20:64.en: So resolve upon your plan and then come [forward] in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes

20:65.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِمَّآ أَن تُلۡقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنۡ أَلۡقَىٰ
20:65.en: They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw

20:66.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ أَلۡقُواْۖ فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمۡ وَعِصِيُّهُمۡ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيۡهِ مِن سِحۡرِهِمۡ أَنَّهَا تَسۡعَىٰ
20:66.en: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving [like snakes]

20:67.en: And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Moses

20:68.ar: قُلۡنَا لَا تَخَفۡ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ
20:68.en: Allah said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior

20:69.ar: وَأَلۡقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ تَلۡقَفۡ مَا صَنَعُوٓاْۖ إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيۡدُ سَٰحِرࣲۖ وَلَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيۡثُ أَتَىٰ
20:69.en: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is

20:70.ar: فَأُلۡقِيَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدࣰ ا قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَٰرُونَ وَمُوسَىٰ
20:70.en: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses

20:71.ar: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمۡ لَهُۥ قَبۡلَ أَنۡ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحۡرَۖ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَرۡجُلَكُم مِّنۡ خِلَٰفࣲ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمۡ فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخۡلِ وَلَتَعۡلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَآ أَشَدُّ عَذَابࣰ ا وَأَبۡقَىٰ
20:71.en: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring

20:72.ar: قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤۡثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَاۖ فَٱقۡضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍۖ إِنَّمَا تَقۡضِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ
20:72.en: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life

20:73.ar: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغۡفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكۡرَهۡتَنَا عَلَيۡهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحۡرِۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓ
20:73.en: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring

20:74.ar: إِنَّهُۥ مَن يَأۡتِ رَبَّهُۥ مُجۡرِمࣰ ا فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحۡيَىٰ
20:74.en: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live

20:75.ar: وَمَن يَأۡتِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنࣰ ا قَدۡ عَمِلَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱلدَّرَجَٰتُ ٱلۡعُلَىٰ
20:75.en: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position]

20:76.ar: جَنَّٰتُ عَدۡنࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ
20:76.en: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself

20:77.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنۡ أَسۡرِ بِعِبَادِي فَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُمۡ طَرِيقࣰ ا فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ يَبَسࣰ ا لَّا تَخَٰفُ دَرَكࣰ ا وَلَا تَخۡشَىٰ
20:77.en: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]

20:78.ar: فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ بِجُنُودِهِۦ فَغَشِيَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡيَمِّ مَا غَشِيَهُمۡ
20:78.en: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them

20:79.en: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them]

20:80.ar: يَٰبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ قَدۡ أَنجَيۡنَٰكُم مِّنۡ عَدُوِّكُمۡ وَوَٰعَدۡنَٰكُمۡ جَانِبَ ٱلطُّورِ ٱلۡأَيۡمَنَ وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَنَّ وَٱلسَّلۡوَىٰ
20:80.en: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails

20:81.ar: كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَلَا تَطۡغَوۡاْ فِيهِ فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَضَبِيۖ وَمَن يَحۡلِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ غَضَبِي فَقَدۡ هَوَىٰ
20:81.en: [Saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress [or oppress others] therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen

20:82.ar: وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارࣱ لِّمَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ
20:82.en: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance

20:83.en: [Allah] said, "And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses

20:84.ar: قَالَ هُمۡ أُوْلَآءِ عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِي وَعَجِلۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ رَبِّ لِتَرۡضَىٰ
20:84.en: He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased

20:85.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَوۡمَكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:85.en: [Allah] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Samiri has led them astray

20:86.ar: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَمۡ يَعِدۡكُمۡ رَبُّكُمۡ وَعۡدًا حَسَنًاۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡعَهۡدُ أَمۡ أَرَدتُّمۡ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَضَبࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُم مَّوۡعِدِي
20:86.en: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me

20:87.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَخۡلَفۡنَا مَوۡعِدَكَ بِمَلۡكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلۡنَآ أَوۡزَارࣰ ا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ فَقَذَفۡنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلۡقَى ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:87.en: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people [of Pharaoh], so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri throw

20:88.ar: فَأَخۡرَجَ لَهُمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارࣱ فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِيَ
20:88.en: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot

20:89.ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوۡنَ أَلَّا يَرۡجِعُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا وَلَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا نَفۡعࣰ ا
20:89.en: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit

20:90.ar: وَلَقَدۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبۡلُ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوٓاْ أَمۡرِي
20:90.en: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order

20:91.ar: قَالُواْ لَن نَّبۡرَحَ عَلَيۡهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرۡجِعَ إِلَيۡنَا مُوسَىٰ
20:91.en: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to the calf until Moses returns to us

20:92.ar: قَالَ يَٰهَٰرُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذۡ رَأَيۡتَهُمۡ ضَلُّوٓاْ
20:92.en: [Moses] said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray

20:93.en: From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order

20:94.ar: قَالَ يَبۡنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأۡخُذۡ بِلِحۡيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأۡسِيٓۖ إِنِّي خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقۡتَ بَيۡنَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمۡ تَرۡقُبۡ قَوۡلِي
20:94.en: [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word

20:95.en: [Moses] said, "And what is your case, O Samiri

20:96.ar: قَالَ بَصُرۡتُ بِمَا لَمۡ يَبۡصُرُواْ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضۡتُ قَبۡضَةࣰ مِّنۡ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذۡتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتۡ لِي نَفۡسِي
20:96.en: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus did my soul entice me

20:97.ar: قَالَ فَٱذۡهَبۡ فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ أَن تَقُولَ لَا مِسَاسَۖ وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوۡعِدࣰ ا لَّن تُخۡلَفَهُۥۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِكَ ٱلَّذِي ظَلۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ عَاكِفࣰ اۖ لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُۥ ثُمَّ لَنَنسِفَنَّهُۥ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ نَسۡفًا
20:97.en: [Moses] said, "Then go. And indeed, it is [decreed] for you in [this] life to say, 'No contact.' And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it into the sea with a blast

20:98.ar: إِنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عِلۡمࣰ ا
20:98.en: Your god is only Allah, except for whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge

20:99.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ أَنۢبَآءِ مَا قَدۡ سَبَقَۚ وَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكَ مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكۡرࣰ ا
20:99.en: Thus, [O Muhammad], We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us the Qur'an

20:100.ar: مَّنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَنۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَحۡمِلُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وِزۡرًا
20:100.en: Whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden

20:101.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهِۖ وَسَآءَ لَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ حِمۡلࣰ ا
20:101.en: [Abiding] eternally therein, and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load

20:102.ar: يَوۡمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِۚ وَنَحۡشُرُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ زُرۡقࣰ ا
20:102.en: The Day the Horn will be blown. And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed

20:103.ar: يَتَخَٰفَتُونَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا عَشۡرࣰ ا
20:103.en: They will murmur among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days in the world]

20:104.ar: نَّحۡنُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذۡ يَقُولُ أَمۡثَلُهُمۡ طَرِيقَةً إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا يَوۡمࣰ ا
20:104.en: We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in manner will say, "You remained not but one day

20:105.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡجِبَالِ فَقُلۡ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسۡفࣰ ا
20:105.en: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast

20:106.en: And He will leave the earth a level plain

20:107.ar: لَّا تَرَىٰ فِيهَا عِوَجࣰ ا وَلَآ أَمۡتࣰ ا
20:107.en: You will not see therein a depression or an elevation

20:108.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِيَ لَا عِوَجَ لَهُۥۖ وَخَشَعَتِ ٱلۡأَصۡوَاتُ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَلَا تَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا هَمۡسࣰ ا
20:108.en: That Day, everyone will follow [the call of] the Caller [with] no deviation therefrom, and [all] voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper [of footsteps]

20:109.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ لَّا تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ إِلَّا مَنۡ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَرَضِيَ لَهُۥ قَوۡلࣰ ا
20:109.en: That Day, no intercession will benefit except [that of] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word

20:110.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣰ ا
20:110.en: Allah knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, but they do not encompass it in knowledge

20:111.ar: ۞وَعَنَتِ ٱلۡوُجُوهُ لِلۡحَيِّ ٱلۡقَيُّومِۖ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنۡ حَمَلَ ظُلۡمࣰ ا
20:111.en: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice

20:112.ar: وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلۡمࣰ ا وَلَا هَضۡمࣰ ا
20:112.en: But he who does of righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation

20:113.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ قُرۡءَانًا عَرَبِيࣰّ ا وَصَرَّفۡنَا فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ أَوۡ يُحۡدِثُ لَهُمۡ ذِكۡرࣰ ا
20:113.en: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it would cause them remembrance

20:114.ar: فَتَعَٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡحَقُّۗ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يُقۡضَىٰٓ إِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهُۥۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدۡنِي عِلۡمࣰ ا
20:114.en: So high [above all] is Allah, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge

20:115.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَهِدۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ ءَادَمَ مِن قَبۡلُ فَنَسِيَ وَلَمۡ نَجِدۡ لَهُۥ عَزۡمࣰ ا
20:115.en: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination

20:116.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ
20:116.en: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees; he refused

20:117.ar: فَقُلۡنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا عَدُوࣱّ لَّكَ وَلِزَوۡجِكَ فَلَا يُخۡرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ فَتَشۡقَىٰٓ
20:117.en: So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer

20:118.ar: إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعۡرَىٰ
20:118.en: Indeed, it is [promised] for you not to be hungry therein or be unclothed

20:119.ar: وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظۡمَؤُاْ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضۡحَىٰ
20:119.en: And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein or be hot from the sun

20:120.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ إِلَيۡهِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَىٰ شَجَرَةِ ٱلۡخُلۡدِ وَمُلۡكࣲ لَّا يَبۡلَىٰ
20:120.en: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate

20:121.ar: فَأَكَلَا مِنۡهَا فَبَدَتۡ لَهُمَا سَوۡءَٰتُهُمَا وَطَفِقَا يَخۡصِفَانِ عَلَيۡهِمَا مِن وَرَقِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۚ وَعَصَىٰٓ ءَادَمُ رَبَّهُۥ فَغَوَىٰ
20:121.en: And Adam and his wife ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred

20:122.ar: ثُمَّ ٱجۡتَبَٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ وَهَدَىٰ
20:122.en: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him]

20:123.ar: قَالَ ٱهۡبِطَا مِنۡهَا جَمِيعَۢاۖ بَعۡضُكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ عَدُوࣱّۖ فَإِمَّا يَأۡتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدࣰ ى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشۡقَىٰ
20:123.en: [Allah] said, "Descend from Paradise - all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter]

20:124.ar: وَمَنۡ أَعۡرَضَ عَن ذِكۡرِي فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ مَعِيشَةࣰ ضَنكࣰ ا وَنَحۡشُرُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ أَعۡمَىٰ
20:124.en: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind

20:125.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرۡتَنِيٓ أَعۡمَىٰ وَقَدۡ كُنتُ بَصِيرࣰ ا
20:125.en: He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I was [once] seeing

20:126.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ أَتَتۡكَ ءَايَٰتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَاۖ وَكَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُنسَىٰ
20:126.en: [Allah] will say, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them; and thus will you this Day be forgotten

20:127.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي مَنۡ أَسۡرَفَ وَلَمۡ يُؤۡمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦۚ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ وَأَبۡقَىٰٓ
20:127.en: And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring

20:130.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِهَاۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآيِٕ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرۡضَىٰ
20:130.en: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied

20:131.ar: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيۡنَيۡكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعۡنَا بِهِۦٓ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ زَهۡرَةَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لِنَفۡتِنَهُمۡ فِيهِۚ وَرِزۡقُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ وَأَبۡقَىٰ
20:131.en: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring

20:132.ar: وَأۡمُرۡ أَهۡلَكَ بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ عَلَيۡهَاۖ لَا نَسۡـَٔلُكَ رِزۡقࣰ اۖ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكَۗ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰ
20:132.en: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those of] righteousness

sRCbUqG_Tew.speaker: adnan
sRCbUqG_Tew.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day series; continues parts 1 and 2 of the same juz in his own voice
sRCbUqG_Tew.title: A Juz A Day: 16th Juz, Part 3 - Surah Taha
sRCbUqG_Tew.one_line: A walk through Surah Taha: Musa's call at the fire, his mission to Pharaoh, the golden calf, Adam, and the closing advice to the Prophet.
sRCbUqG_Tew.summary: This third part of the sixteenth juz covers Surah Taha, which he presents as a surah that spends most of its length on the story of Musa from the moment revelation begins. He opens with the reassurance that the Quran was not sent to cause distress, then follows Musa at the fire: Allah, established on His throne and not contained by the world, speaks to him, sets out the etiquette of the sacred valley, tells him he was chosen for the good in him, and gives the core message. He stresses that prayer exists for the remembrance of Allah, so a prayer that does not bring Allah to mind misses its mark. He dwells on Musa's dua for an open heart, an easy task, a loosened tongue and his brother's help, on the love with which Allah raised Musa, on speaking gently even to a tyrant, and on Musa's very human fear before the magicians. Harun's restraint with the calf worshippers is read as wisdom to avoid splitting the people. The closing passages turn to the Day of Judgment, the shortness of worldly life, the miserable life of those who turn from the reminder, and the command to be patient, glorify Allah, keep praying and not crave what others enjoy.

outline.heading: Opening
The Quran was not sent to cause distress
outline.gist: The surah opens by describing the Quran as a reminder from the Creator of the heavens and earth who knows the secret and what is even more hidden.

outline.heading: A surah devoted to the story of Musa
outline.gist: He notes that verses 9 to 99 tell Musa's story in unusual detail, starting from the moment he receives revelation.

outline.heading: Called from the fire in the sacred valley
outline.gist: Musa sees a fire and is addressed by his Lord; Allah is established on His throne yet speaks to him from the fire, tells him to remove his sandals and that he has been chosen.

outline.heading: Prayer for remembrance and the hidden Hour
outline.gist: The purpose of salah is to remember Allah and carry that into life; the Hour is kept hidden so each soul is rewarded for its effort, and desires must not distract from it.

outline.heading: The staff becomes a serpent and the shining hand
outline.gist: Allah asks about the staff He already knows, to show Musa that what he thinks he knows will become a sign; then the hand comes out white, and he is sent to Pharaoh.

outline.heading: Musa's dua for an open heart and a helper
outline.gist: Musa asks for an uplifted heart, an easy task, a loosened tongue and his brother Harun as support, so they can glorify Allah together; he notes teachers open lessons with this dua.

outline.heading: Favours from before: the basket, the sister, the escape
outline.gist: Allah recounts how He saved the infant Musa, returned him to his mother, saved him after the killing, and raised him under His care and love for His service.

outline.heading: Go with My signs and speak gently
outline.gist: Musa and Harun are told to hold to remembrance as things get hard and to speak gently to a tyrant in the hope that he takes heed.

outline.heading: Facing Pharaoh: who is your Lord?
outline.gist: Allah reassures them He is with them; before Pharaoh they demand freedom for the Israelites and describe their Lord as the One who gave everything its form and guided it.

outline.heading: The contest and Musa's human fear
outline.gist: The appointment is set on the festival day so all can witness; Musa feels fear facing a cheering crowd, and Allah tells him to cast the staff because their trick cannot succeed.

outline.heading: The magicians believe and face Pharaoh's threat
outline.gist: The magicians prostrate and accept faith at once despite the threat of crucifixion; Allah contrasts hell for the evildoer with the gardens for those who purify themselves.

outline.heading: The exodus and the blessings on the Israelites
outline.gist: Pharaoh's people drown and the Israelites are reminded of the appointment at the mount, the manna and quails, and the warning not to transgress.

outline.heading: Hastening to the meeting and the golden calf
outline.gist: Musa comes early to meet his Lord, a sign that what matters is met on time; meanwhile the Samiri makes a lowing calf from the people's gold.

outline.heading: Harun's restraint to avoid dividing the people
outline.gist: Harun explains he held back so as not to split the Israelites into warring groups; the Samiri is cast out and the idol destroyed to show it is falsehood.

outline.heading: The Day of Judgment and the shortness of this life
outline.gist: People will guess they stayed ten days or one; voices will be hushed and only permitted intercession will help, so prepare and do not be consumed by this life.

outline.heading: An Arabic Quran and 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge'
outline.gist: The warnings are varied so people may be mindful, and the Prophet is told not to rush the revelation and to ask for more knowledge.

outline.heading: Adam, guidance, and the blindness of turning away
outline.gist: Whoever follows guidance will not go astray or suffer; whoever turns away has a miserable life and is raised blind, having been blind to the revelation.

outline.heading: Patience, glorification, prayer and not craving the world
outline.gist: The surah closes by telling the Prophet to be patient, glorify Allah through the day, keep his family praying and not crave the fleeting splendour given to others.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: The life of Musa from his call at the fire to the golden calf, read for what it teaches about being chosen and carrying a message.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Salah is for remembering Allah; a prayer that does not bring Him to mind misses its purpose.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Musa's dua for an open heart, an easy task, clear speech and a helper, which he recommends before any lesson.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Even a tyrant like Pharaoh is to be addressed gently in the hope he takes heed.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: Harun held back to avoid splitting the people into two warring camps, which he presents as wisdom.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The hushed Day of Judgment and how short worldly life will seem, so prepare rather than be consumed by it.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: Following guidance protects in both lives; turning from the reminder brings a miserable life and blindness on the Day.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Do not let the eyes crave the fleeting splendour others are tested with; what Allah provides in the hereafter is better.

maxims: A salah that does not make us remember Allah misses the mark
When something is important, you are there early for it

stories.point: Allah chose him for the goodness in him and gave him the core message of tawhid and prayer.

stories.who: Musa's infancy in the basket and his sister
stories.point: Allah raised him under His own care and love before ever giving him the mission.
Even a prophet feels fear facing the crowd and the status quo; Allah's support outweighs the spectacle of falsehood.
He held back to prevent division, a reasoned choice rather than weakness.
Guidance will come; whoever follows it is safe and whoever turns away is blind on the Day.

takeaways: Let your prayer actually bring Allah to mind and carry that remembrance into the rest of the day
Make Musa's dua for an open heart and clear speech before teaching or hard tasks
Speak gently even to those who oppose you
Be early and on time for what matters to Allah
Be patient with hurtful words, keep praying and do not crave what others have in this world

20:85.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَوۡمَكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:85.en: [Allah] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Samiri has led them astray

20:86.ar: فَرَجَعَ مُوسَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ غَضۡبَٰنَ أَسِفࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَمۡ يَعِدۡكُمۡ رَبُّكُمۡ وَعۡدًا حَسَنًاۚ أَفَطَالَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡعَهۡدُ أَمۡ أَرَدتُّمۡ أَن يَحِلَّ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَضَبࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ فَأَخۡلَفۡتُم مَّوۡعِدِي
20:86.en: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me

20:87.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَخۡلَفۡنَا مَوۡعِدَكَ بِمَلۡكِنَا وَلَٰكِنَّا حُمِّلۡنَآ أَوۡزَارࣰ ا مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ فَقَذَفۡنَٰهَا فَكَذَٰلِكَ أَلۡقَى ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:87.en: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people [of Pharaoh], so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Samiri throw

20:88.ar: فَأَخۡرَجَ لَهُمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارࣱ فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِيَ
20:88.en: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot

20:89.ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوۡنَ أَلَّا يَرۡجِعُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا وَلَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا نَفۡعࣰ ا
20:89.en: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit

20:90.ar: وَلَقَدۡ قَالَ لَهُمۡ هَٰرُونُ مِن قَبۡلُ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنتُم بِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ فَٱتَّبِعُونِي وَأَطِيعُوٓاْ أَمۡرِي
20:90.en: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order

20:91.ar: قَالُواْ لَن نَّبۡرَحَ عَلَيۡهِ عَٰكِفِينَ حَتَّىٰ يَرۡجِعَ إِلَيۡنَا مُوسَىٰ
20:91.en: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to the calf until Moses returns to us

21:51.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ ءَاتَيۡنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ رُشۡدَهُۥ مِن قَبۡلُ وَكُنَّا بِهِۦ عَٰلِمِينَ
21:51.en: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before, and We were of him well-Knowing

21:52.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلتَّمَاثِيلُ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنتُمۡ لَهَا عَٰكِفُونَ
21:52.en: When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted

21:53.en: They said, "We found our fathers worshippers of them

21:54.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُمۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
21:54.en: He said, "You were certainly, you and your fathers, in manifest error

21:55.ar: قَالُوٓاْ أَجِئۡتَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ أَمۡ أَنتَ مِنَ ٱللَّٰعِبِينَ
21:55.en: They said, "Have you come to us with truth, or are you of those who jest

21:56.ar: قَالَ بَل رَّبُّكُمۡ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ وَأَنَا۠ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ
21:56.en: He said, "[No], rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I, to that, am of those who testify

21:57.ar: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصۡنَٰمَكُم بَعۡدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدۡبِرِينَ
21:57.en: And [I swear] by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away

21:58.ar: فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ يَرۡجِعُونَ
21:58.en: So he made them into fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it [and question]

21:59.ar: قَالُواْ مَن فَعَلَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَآ إِنَّهُۥ لَمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
21:59.en: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers

21:60.ar: قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا فَتࣰ ى يَذۡكُرُهُمۡ يُقَالُ لَهُۥٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمُ
21:60.en: They said, "We heard a young man mention them who is called Abraham

21:61.ar: قَالُواْ فَأۡتُواْ بِهِۦ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡيُنِ ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡهَدُونَ
21:61.en: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify

21:62.ar: قَالُوٓاْ ءَأَنتَ فَعَلۡتَ هَٰذَا بِـَٔالِهَتِنَا يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ
21:62.en: They said, "Have you done this to our gods, O Abraham

21:63.ar: قَالَ بَلۡ فَعَلَهُۥ كَبِيرُهُمۡ هَٰذَا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُمۡ إِن كَانُواْ يَنطِقُونَ
21:63.en: He said, "Rather, this - the largest of them - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak

21:64.ar: فَرَجَعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ فَقَالُوٓاْ إِنَّكُمۡ أَنتُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
21:64.en: So they returned to [blaming] themselves and said [to each other], "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers

21:65.ar: ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمۡ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
21:65.en: Then they reversed themselves, [saying], "You have already known that these do not speak

21:66.ar: قَالَ أَفَتَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ
21:66.en: He said, "Then do you worship instead of Allah that which does not benefit you at all or harm you

21:67.ar: أُفࣲّ لَّكُمۡ وَلِمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
21:67.en: Uff to you and to what you worship instead of Allah. Then will you not use reason

21:68.ar: قَالُواْ حَرِّقُوهُ وَٱنصُرُوٓاْ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ فَٰعِلِينَ
21:68.en: They said, "Burn him and support your gods - if you are to act

22:11.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
22:11.en: And of the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [to the other direction]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss

22:12.ar: يَدۡعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَضُرُّهُۥ وَمَا لَا يَنفَعُهُۥۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَٰلُ ٱلۡبَعِيدُ
22:12.en: He invokes instead of Allah that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is what is the extreme error

22:13.ar: يَدۡعُواْ لَمَن ضَرُّهُۥٓ أَقۡرَبُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِۦۚ لَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَلَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡعَشِيرُ
22:13.en: He invokes one whose harm is closer than his benefit - how wretched the protector and how wretched the associate

7:138.ar: وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ يَعۡكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصۡنَامࣲ لَّهُمۡۚ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجۡعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهࣰ ا كَمَا لَهُمۡ ءَالِهَةࣱۚ قَالَ إِنَّكُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ تَجۡهَلُونَ
7:138.en: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea; then they came upon a people intent in devotion to [some] idols of theirs. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly

37:89.en: And said, "Indeed, I am [about to be] ill

17:81.ar: وَقُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُۚ إِنَّ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ كَانَ زَهُوقࣰ ا
17:81.en: And say, "Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to depart

t0OcFedj33s.speaker: adnan
t0OcFedj33s.speaker_note: Sh. Adnan's Ramadan halqa series; speaks of his own years of study and his minbar in the community
t0OcFedj33s.title: Exposing Irrationality (Ramadan 2026, Night 16: Quranic Themes 2)
t0OcFedj33s.one_line: How the Quran exposes irrational beliefs, from the golden calf and Ibrahim's idols to conditional worship, and why ideas must change at the root.
t0OcFedj33s.summary: He begins with how baseless ideas spread from one loud voice into unquestioned norms. Truth wins in the end, but slowly. Superstitions, astrology and belief in jinn steering people's minds have no evidence, yet parents still take children to exorcists, and correcting such irrationalities is the minbar's job, which only works if people question what they inherited. The Quran exposes irrationality with simple questions. Bani Israel, after every miracle and the parted sea, worshipped a lowing golden calf, and the Quran asks whether they could not see it gives no answer and has no power to harm or benefit; he compares people pleading at shrines where no one is buried. Centuries of decline left Muslims with defeated ideas and severe literalism, where a teenager with one hadith from YouTube lectures a scholar. Ibrahim kept his reason as a child, broke the idols and told his people to ask the largest one; they saw the truth for a moment and then burned him anyway. The Prophet never broke the Ka'bah's idols in Mecca; he spent twenty years changing minds until the idols fell when he pointed at them. Muslims must first fix their own false certainties, which drive youth away. Finally, worshipping Allah only when things go well loses both this world and the next.

outline.heading: How baseless ideas become norms
outline.gist: One popular or powerful voice backed by key people can turn an absurd, evidence-free idea into public opinion and then an unquestioned maxim.

outline.heading: Truth prevails, but slowly
outline.gist: Muslims believe the stronger idea, the truth, eventually wins and falsehood is discarded, but it does not happen automatically.

outline.heading: Superstitions and astrology
outline.gist: Not walking under ladders and believing planets decide your fate are baseless ideas that have floated for centuries and are hard to remove.

outline.heading: Jinn possession and exorcisms
outline.gist: Muslims have superstitions too, such as a jinn sitting in the brain steering a person; there is no evidence for it, yet after he explains this people still take their children to exorcists. Correcting such ideas is the masjid's main job.

outline.heading: Critical thinking comes first
outline.gist: Unless people are willing to question themselves and what they inherited from parents and society, there is little hope of changing minds; the Quran exposes irrationality elegantly.

outline.heading: Miracle after miracle for a hard-headed people
outline.gist: Bani Israel saw the staff, the shining hand and the plagues that struck only the Egyptians, then crossed the sea and watched Pharaoh drown.

outline.heading: Their feet still wet from the sea
outline.gist: Musa leaves for a few days and is told the Samiri has misled them; he returns angry and sad, asking whether the promise seemed too long in coming.

outline.heading: The golden calf that made a sound
outline.gist: The Samiri made a lowing golden calf and they called it Musa's god, forgetting nine miracles; raised among Egyptian pagans, they wanted a shiny god like everyone else.

outline.heading: 'Do they not see it cannot answer them?'
outline.gist: The Quran exposes the calf simply: it cannot speak, harm or benefit them, and has no power over anything.

outline.heading: A visible god should at least do what you can
outline.gist: If you worship something present before you, it should at least communicate and have power you lack; the calf does nothing for them.

outline.heading: Shrines with no one buried in them
outline.gist: People rub themselves on graves and leave money asking for marriages and houses, even at shrines where no one is buried, because ideas are so hard to dislodge.

outline.heading: The Prophet changed ideas first
outline.gist: His miracle was changing ideas before anything else; centuries of decline have left Muslims with ideas that belong to a defeated population, not to Islam.

outline.heading: Literalism comes from intellectual defeat
outline.gist: Severe literalism thrives where people are intellectually bankrupt; a youth who reads one hadith online lectures scholars, which no other discipline would tolerate.

outline.heading: Start with the simple irrationalities
outline.gist: He once argued with a fourteen-year-old over a term he studied for twenty-five years without being permitted to use; the Quran's method is to begin with basic questions.

outline.heading: Harun explained, but they waited for Musa
outline.gist: Harun, the scholar, explained everything, but they would only listen to Musa, whom they feared.

outline.heading: Ibrahim held on to his reason
outline.gist: As a child Ibrahim refused the inherited lies about idols; Allah helped him, since children usually cannot withstand such a flood of ideas.

outline.heading: Staying behind from the festival
outline.gist: His arguments only annoyed people, so he said he was sick and stayed behind when everyone left for their celebration.

outline.heading: Breaking the idols
outline.gist: He told the idols to eat and speak, smashed them and left the axe in the hand of the largest; the people returned and summoned him.

outline.heading: 'Ask them, if they can speak'
outline.gist: He blamed the biggest idol; for a moment they turned to themselves and admitted they were the wrongdoers.

outline.heading: Turned on their heads
outline.gist: They flipped back, thinking upside down, and said he knew idols cannot speak; he asked why they worship what cannot help or harm them.

outline.heading: Burning the one who 'killed their gods'
outline.gist: They threw him into an enormous fire for killing their gods, an absurd sentence; exposing their irrationality did not change them, and he was driven out.

outline.heading: The Prophet never broke the idols in Mecca
outline.gist: With over 360 idols around the Ka'bah, he never sent anyone to break one; he had learned from Ibrahim and spent twenty years striving to change minds.

outline.heading: Change the idea and the idol falls
outline.gist: At the conquest he recited an ayah and pointed, and the idols fell by themselves; debunking a symbol does not change the root idea.

outline.heading: Breaking symbols creates martyrs
outline.gist: Smashing idols hands their followers propaganda and sympathy; change the mind that gives them meaning and they fade away. Ibrahim, young, exposed the irrationality perfectly, but ideas do not change that way.

outline.heading: First fix our own false certainties
outline.gist: When parents bring him children who have left Islam, they have often been fed misconceptions for so long that nothing he says can reach them.

outline.heading: Stop taking your kids to exorcists
outline.gist: Parents only know the Islam they were told; he has preached against jinn removal for years, yet people still take children to men who beat them to drive a jinn out.

outline.heading: Spread Islam's proper ideas
outline.gist: To spread Islam we must change how we understand the world and ourselves and spread its proper ethics, values and understanding; there is a long way to go.

outline.heading: Worshipping Allah on the edge
outline.gist: Some worship Allah at the edge of a cliff: content when they are healthy and wealthy, and falling away the moment hardship comes.

outline.heading: Losing this world and the next
outline.gist: Turning bitter and leaving the faith in hardship does not improve worldly life and costs the hereafter; then they call on what can neither harm nor help them.

outline.heading: Conditional worship makes no sense
outline.gist: What they call on harms more than it helps; you worship Allah because He is Allah, and worship Him more when you do not get what you want.

outline.heading: A child's tantrum
outline.gist: Abandoning faith over a hardship is like a four-year-old who breaks his toy when told no; persevere so at least your hereafter is safe.

outline.heading: Meet hardship and win both
outline.gist: Even on logic alone, losing both worlds is absurd; facing difficulty with optimism and effort brings contentment now and reward later.

themes.label: Conspiracy thinking and critical thinking
themes.note: Baseless ideas spread into unquestioned norms; superstitions and astrology survive because people do not question what they inherit.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Belief in jinn controlling the mind and the practice of exorcism have no basis in the deen.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Musa's people worship a golden calf after every miracle, and the Quran exposes the irrationality with a simple question.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: What cannot speak, harm or benefit cannot be worshipped, whether a calf or an empty shrine.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Severe literalism and arguing from a single hadith reflect intellectual defeat and disregard for the depth of Islamic scholarship.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim keeps his reason, breaks the idols and exposes his people, who burn him anyway.

themes.label: Reform (islah)
themes.note: The Prophet changed ideas at the root rather than attacking symbols; Muslims must first correct their own false certainties.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people leave Islam after being fed misconceptions presented as the deen.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Conditional faith that collapses in hardship loses both worlds; perseverance wins both.

quran.point: Bani Israel asked Musa to make them a god like the gods of others.
Ibrahim says he is sick so he can stay behind from the festival.
Truth has come and falsehood has perished, recited as the idols fell at the conquest of Mecca.

hadith.gist: At the conquest of Mecca the Prophet, on his mount, recited an ayah and pointed at each idol around the Ka'bah, and it fell over by itself.
hadith.source: Sirat Ibn Hisham, from Ibn Abbas

maxims: If you change the idea, the idol will fall by itself
He changed ideas before he changed anything else
Severe literalism exists only in intellectually defeated societies
If you don't get what you want, worship Allah more
Don't worship God with one foot here and one there
Face hardship and you win both

stories.who: Bani Israel and the golden calf
stories.point: Even after countless miracles, people cling to the irrational ideas they grew up with.
Islamic knowledge is deep; reading one hadith online does not make anyone a scholar.
Exposing irrationality was right, but breaking symbols did not change minds.

stories.who: The idols falling at the conquest of Mecca
stories.point: Change the idea at the root and its symbols collapse on their own.

contemporary: Astrology on television and in newspapers
Superstitions such as not walking under ladders
Exorcism films and jinn-removal practices in Muslim communities
Shrines and graves visited for wishes
Young people arguing religion from a hadith found on YouTube

takeaways: Question inherited beliefs and practise critical thinking.
Stop taking children to exorcists and jinn removers.
Respect the depth of Islamic scholarship instead of arguing from a single text found online.
Change people's ideas at the root through patient teaching rather than attacking symbols.
Worship Allah unconditionally and meet hardship with perseverance so you do not lose both worlds.

25:77.ar: قُلۡ مَا يَعۡبَؤُاْ بِكُمۡ رَبِّي لَوۡلَا دُعَآؤُكُمۡۖ فَقَدۡ كَذَّبۡتُمۡ فَسَوۡفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامَۢا
25:77.en: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication?" For you [disbelievers] have denied, so your denial is going to be adherent

26:77.ar: فَإِنَّهُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ لِّيٓ إِلَّا رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
26:77.en: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds

26:78.en: Who created me, and He [it is who] guides me

26:79.en: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink

26:80.en: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me

26:81.en: And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life

26:82.ar: وَٱلَّذِيٓ أَطۡمَعُ أَن يَغۡفِرَ لِي خَطِيٓـَٔتِي يَوۡمَ ٱلدِّينِ
26:82.en: And who I aspire that He will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense

27:19.ar: فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكࣰ ا مِّن قَوۡلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَدۡخِلۡنِي بِرَحۡمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

12:101.ar: ۞رَبِّ قَدۡ ءَاتَيۡتَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُلۡكِ وَعَلَّمۡتَنِي مِن تَأۡوِيلِ ٱلۡأَحَادِيثِۚ فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَنتَ وَلِيِّۦ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ تَوَفَّنِي مُسۡلِمࣰ ا وَأَلۡحِقۡنِي بِٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ

mbWA7IFdIVI.speaker: adnan
mbWA7IFdIVI.speaker_note: single speaker in the sheikh's Ramadan nightly Quranic Themes series; refers to his own teachers and the reciters he trains
mbWA7IFdIVI.title: Ramadan 2026 Night 18: Supplications
mbWA7IFdIVI.one_line: Dua as our side of a conversation Allah began, drawn from Al-Furqan 25:77 and the supplications of Ibrahim and Sulayman.
mbWA7IFdIVI.summary: He frames dua as the brain of every act of worship and as our reply to a conversation Allah started through the Quran, a book that never goes stale the way even great human literature does. He warns against treating dua as Aladdin's lamp, since faith built on getting wishes granted collapses the first time a request is refused. The closing verse of Al-Furqan says Allah would not care for us at all were it not for our dua; he defends this by asking listeners to take Allah's perspective: a vast universe made from nothing, a single welcoming planet, the gift of intellect, and still most people never turn to the One behind it. He then studies Ibrahim's words on leaving Babylon, disowned by his father: he asks not for victory or wealth but for sound judgment, to be joined with the righteous, a truthful tongue, forgiveness for his father, and a sound heart. Prophets praying for those who harmed them, including the Prophet at Uhud, show the same mercy. Sulayman and Yusuf, at the height of power, ask only for gratitude and to be counted among the righteous, proving humility lives in the heart. He urges people to ask, for the rest of Ramadan, for what really matters.

outline.heading: Opening
Dua as a building block inside every act of worship
outline.gist: Acts like salah are built from smaller pieces such as invocation, recitation and submission, and dua runs through all of them.

outline.heading: Dua is worship: speaking back to the One who spoke first
outline.gist: The hadith call dua worship and the brain of worship; without it rituals are mechanics. Allah opened the conversation with 604 pages.

outline.heading: The Quran: a conversation that never expires
outline.gist: Almost no book stays relevant for centuries; even Shakespeare is hard to justify teaching to teenagers today, while the Quran still guides after 1400 years.

outline.heading: Every word read, defended and practised
outline.gist: Unlike traditions that study only selected chapters, Muslims recite and live every word, and the Quran set out an ethically coherent framework the social sciences are only now approaching.

outline.heading: Dua is not Aladdin's lamp
outline.gist: Treating dua as a wish machine is materialistic; he has seen people embrace Islam over one answered dua, and that understanding can break faith when a dua is not answered.

outline.heading: Ya'ba': to care is to carry someone
outline.gist: The verse asks what your Lord would care for you without your dua; the root word means a burden, because caring for someone means carrying them in your thoughts and worry.

outline.heading: Without dua you are insignificant: see it from His side
outline.gist: This is not harsh once you try Allah's perspective: He made time and a universe measured in hundreds of millions of light years from nothing.

outline.heading: One welcoming planet and the gift of intellect
outline.gist: Out of 13 billion years and a hostile cosmos, we alone can reason and reflect on our existence, and even a basic life is an extraordinary gift.

outline.heading: Uninterested in the One who gave us everything
outline.gist: Most people never ask who is behind their life or thank Him; pain exists so that we can recognise sweetness and health at all.

outline.heading: Dua: opening your whole heart to Allah
outline.gist: After revelation and a final messenger people still do not speak to Him; dua means sharing fears, hopes, regrets and plans, and the verse ends with a warning to those who deny.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's dua: only the Lord of the worlds
outline.gist: He renders Ibrahim's words: the Lord who creates, guides, feeds, heals, gives death and life and forgives; then the requests, with two valid readings of a truthful tongue among later generations.

outline.heading: Hukm: asking for good judgment, not power
outline.gist: Said as Ibrahim walks out of Babylon; hukm here is sound judgment, the ability to choose rightly when temptation, relationships and fear of loss cloud the decision.

outline.heading: We ask for stuff; he asked for judgment in exile
outline.gist: People ask for degrees, spouses and houses; Ibrahim, expelled and disowned, did not ask for victory or revenge but to keep making choices that please Allah.

outline.heading: Join me with the righteous, and forgive my father
outline.gist: He wants simply to be let in with the righteous, to have a tongue that speaks the truth before Allah, and forgiveness for the father who threw him out.

outline.heading: The prophet who prayed for the people who struck him
outline.gist: The Prophet described an earlier prophet wiping blood from his face while asking Allah to forgive his people for they did not know.

outline.heading: Uhud: the Prophet refuses to curse his people
outline.gist: Wounded, having lost Hamza and many companions, he is asked to pray against Quraysh; the companions regret asking, and he prays for their guidance instead.

outline.heading: A sound heart on the Day nothing else counts
outline.gist: On a Day when wealth and children do not help, only a heart free of arrogance, envy, hatred, selfishness and shirk will matter.

outline.heading: Sulayman: a kingdom no one has had since
outline.gist: He rode the wind, ruled people, jinn, birds and insects, and was a prophet son of a prophet; there was nothing left in the world to wish for.

outline.heading: Sulayman's dua: gratitude and being counted among the righteous
outline.gist: He asks only to be able to thank Allah for what he and his parents were given, to use it to please Him, and by His mercy to be entered among the righteous.

outline.heading: Humility lives inside: Yusuf at the height of power
outline.gist: Some early Muslims and some of his teachers kept a poor appearance to stay humble, but Yusuf, given rule and knowledge, still asks to die Muslim and be joined with the righteous; wealth and status can sit with a humble heart.

outline.heading: Ask for what matters this Ramadan
outline.gist: The prophets mean these requests sincerely; for the rest of the month ask for good judgment, truthfulness, good ethics and a place among the righteous.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Dua is the core of worship and our reply to Allah's conversation with us, not a wish machine whose failure breaks faith.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is a living divine communication that stays relevant across centuries and is practised in every word.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Seeing creation from Allah's side shows why a person who never turns to Him has no claim on His care.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Even someone unsure of God should want to thank whoever gave them life; hardship lets us recognise blessings.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Ibrahim's requests in exile model asking for judgment, truthfulness and belonging with the righteous rather than possessions.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Ibrahim, an earlier prophet and the Prophet at Uhud all prayed for the guidance of those who hurt them.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: The sound heart, free of arrogance, envy and selfishness, is the only thing that counts on the Day of Judgment.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Sulayman and Yusuf show that humility is an inner state, compatible with power and wealth.

quran.point: Yusuf, given rule and knowledge, asks only to die Muslim and be joined with the righteous: humility at the height of power.

hadith.gist: Dua is worship.
Dua is the brain (core) of worship.
The Prophet told of an earlier prophet whose people beat him until he bled, and who wiped the blood away saying: O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.
At Uhud, wounded and asked to pray against Quraysh, the Prophet prayed for their guidance instead.

maxims: Dua is your conversation with the divine
Dua is not Aladdin's lamp
When you care about someone, you carry them
Ask for what matters
Humbleness and purity exist inside

stories.who: Converts whose faith rested on one answered dua
stories.point: Faith built on getting what you ask for breaks when a request is refused.

stories.who: Ibrahim leaving Babylon, disowned by his father
stories.point: In exile he asks for good judgment and forgiveness for his father rather than victory or wealth.

stories.who: An earlier prophet beaten by his people
stories.point: Praying for the forgiveness of those who harm you is the prophetic way.
Even after terrible losses he would not curse his people and prayed for their guidance.
With every worldly blessing, his only request was gratitude and a place among the righteous.
Power and knowledge did not dent his humility; he asked to die Muslim.

contemporary: Debate among educators about continuing to teach Shakespeare in schools
takeaways: Treat dua as an ongoing conversation with Allah about your fears, hopes, regrets and plans, not a wish list.
For the rest of Ramadan ask for good judgment, truthfulness, good ethics and to be joined with the righteous.
Pray for the guidance of people who wrong you instead of against them.
Work on a heart free of arrogance, envy and selfishness, since that is what counts on the Day of Judgment.
Stay humble inwardly whatever your wealth or status, seeing all of it as Allah's blessing.

8:62.ar: وَإِن يُرِيدُوٓاْ أَن يَخۡدَعُوكَ فَإِنَّ حَسۡبَكَ ٱللَّهُۚ هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَيَّدَكَ بِنَصۡرِهِۦ وَبِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
